pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these do plants need to stay alive? (1 mark)
   A. Only darkness
   B. Stones and plastic
   C. Water, air and light
   D. Only sand

2. A student says a tree is not alive because it does not move from place to place. What is wrong with this idea? (1 mark)
   A. Trees are made of stone
   B. Plants show life by growing and responding
   C. Only animals grow
   D. Trees are not plants

3. What is the word for the tiny parts in a leaf where air goes in and out? (1 mark)
   A. Petals
   B. Tiny holes
   C. Roots
   D. Seeds

4. What does a snail do when you touch it? (1 mark)
   A. Grows a tail
   B. Starts to sing
   C. Flies away
   D. Pulls its body into its shell

5. Which of these can cause stomach ache? (1 mark)
   A. Drinking clean water
   B. Brushing teeth
   C. Washing hands
   D. Eating too fast or germs in dirty food

6. What does deworming do? (1 mark)
   A. Makes food taste better
   B. Cleans teeth
   C. Kills worms in the intestines
   D. Cures a cough

7. Where does the digestive tube end? (1 mark)
   A. Mouth
   B. Gullet
   C. Stomach
   D. Anus

8. What is the correct order of parts food passes through? (1 mark)
   A. Mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine
   B. Mouth, stomach, gullet, anus
   C. Gullet, mouth, small intestine, stomach
   D. Stomach, mouth, gullet, small intestine

9. Which of these is true of a liquid? (1 mark)
   A. It fills a room
   B. It has no volume
   C. It has a fixed shape but no fixed volume
   D. It has a fixed volume but no fixed shape

10. Which of these gases do we breathe in to stay alive? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fumes
   B. Dust
   C. Oxygen
   D. Smoke

11. What does volume mean? (1 mark)
   A. How heavy it feels
   B. The colour of an object
   C. The amount of matter in an object
   D. The amount of space an object takes up

12. Why are liquids useful for drinking? (1 mark)
   A. They can be poured and swallowed
   B. They cannot flow
   C. They are always hot
   D. They keep their own shape

13. A bag has 1 kg of rice and 250 g of beans. What is the total mass? (1 mark)
   A. 1250 g
   B. 350 g
   C. 2500 g
   D. 1025 g

14. Which state of matter has no fixed shape and no fixed volume? (1 mark)
   A. Liquid
   B. Powder
   C. Gas
   D. Solid

15. Why is it good to separate waste into different bins? (1 mark)
   A. It makes waste burn
   B. It makes waste smell
   C. It makes reusing, recycling and composting easier
   D. It makes waste heavier

16. What is decomposable waste? (1 mark)
   A. Waste made of plastic
   B. Waste that rots and breaks down
   C. Waste made of metal
   D. Waste that never changes

17. Which of these is a danger of solid waste? (1 mark)
   A. It makes air fresh
   B. It grows food
   C. It cleans rivers
   D. It blocks drains and causes floods

18. Why are gumboots useful when handling waste? (1 mark)
   A. They make waste lighter
   B. They protect the feet from sharp things and dirt
   C. They make hands clean
   D. They make waste rot

19. Which is an example of reducing waste? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving litter at a picnic
   B. Carrying a cloth shopping bag
   C. Burning plastic
   D. Throwing a bottle in a river

20. Which of these is a way to save water when bathing? (1 mark)
   A. Use a hose
   B. Use a sprinkler
   C. Use a basin
   D. Leave the tap open

21. A dripping tap fills a 5 litre bucket in one day. How much water is wasted in 4 days? (1 mark)
   A. 1 litre
   B. 20 litres
   C. 54 litres
   D. 9 litres

22. What does drip irrigation do? (1 mark)
   A. Cleans the soil
   B. Makes rain
   C. Gives water to each plant a drop at a time
   D. Floods the whole field

23. What is a good message for a water conservation poster? (1 mark)
   A. Leave the tap open
   B. Water is free for all to waste
   C. Close the tap after use
   D. Waste is fun

24. A tap leaks 3 litres each hour. How much is wasted in one day of 24 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 27 litres
   B. 48 litres
   C. 24 litres
   D. 72 litres

25. Why must we conserve water? (1 mark)
   A. Water is not needed
   B. Water never ends
   C. Water is always free
   D. Fresh water is limited

26. Which of these can make a river dry up? (1 mark)
   A. Planting trees
   B. Cutting trees near it and wasting water
   C. Saving water
   D. Using rain tanks

27. Why is a bucket better than a running tap for washing a bicycle? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the bicycle dirty
   B. It makes it heavier
   C. It uses more water
   D. It uses less water

28. Which of these describes recycling water? (1 mark)
   A. Letting water evaporate
   B. Boiling it and throwing it
   C. Wasting water
   D. Cleaning used water so it can be used again

29. What happens when you push a book gently with a finger compared with a hard push? (1 mark)
   A. It does not move with the hard push
   B. It moves faster with the gentle push
   C. It moves slowly with the gentle push
   D. It flies away with the gentle push

30. A ball is rolling and you kick it in the direction it moves. What happens? (1 mark)
   A. It changes into a solid
   B. It stops
   C. It gets smaller
   D. It speeds up

31. A wheelbarrow is easier to move than dragging a load because (1 mark)
   A. The wheel is heavy
   B. The load gets smaller
   C. The wheel reduces friction
   D. Gravity is less

32. Which of these is a torch used for? (1 mark)
   A. To give light in the dark
   B. To make food
   C. To make sound
   D. To cool a room

33. Which small living thing makes its own light and so is a natural source? (1 mark)
   A. Candle
   B. Torch
   C. Electric bulb
   D. Firefly

34. Which of these is an artificial way of lighting a house? (1 mark)
   A. Electric bulbs
   B. Windows
   C. Sun through the door
   D. Moonlight

35. What do reflectors on a road or bicycle do? (1 mark)
   A. Make heat
   B. Make sound
   C. Make their own light all night
   D. Shine when car lights fall on them

36. The moon shines brightly at night. Why is it still not a source of light? (1 mark)
   A. It is too near
   B. It reflects light from the sun
   C. It is cold
   D. It is too small

37. Which of these helps to prevent burns? (1 mark)
   A. Playing near fire
   B. Holding hot handles
   C. Touching hot pots
   D. Using gloves

38. Why does hot tea cool down? (1 mark)
   A. It loses heat to the air and cup
   B. It gains light
   C. It becomes heavier
   D. It gains cold

39. What does a mother hen do for her chicks? (1 mark)
   A. Cools them
   B. Keeps them warm under her wings
   C. Makes them wet
   D. Feeds them iron

40. Why do farmers dry maize in the sun before storing it? (1 mark)
   A. So it becomes heavier
   B. So it does not rot or grow mould
   C. So it becomes wetter
   D. So it starts to grow

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Discuss how a family can light their home cheaply and safely. (5 marks)

42. Classify these as natural or artificial: candle, stars, torch, lightning, firefly, solar lamp. (4 marks)

43. Give three safety measures during waste management. (3 marks)

44. Describe how to make a pair of kitchen gloves from local materials. (4 marks)

45. Describe an activity that shows the uses of heat, for example drying clothes in different conditions. (5 marks)

46. A pupil wants to find out which material is transparent, translucent or opaque. Describe a test. (4 marks)

47. Explain why sand is not a liquid although it can be poured. (3 marks)

48. Describe the journey of a mouthful of food from the mouth to the anus. (4 marks)

49. State two reasons for conserving water. (2 marks)

50. Explain why sorting waste is important for reusing and recycling. (4 marks)

51. Give three safety rules when using sources of light. (3 marks)

52. What is the difference between a vertebrate and an invertebrate? (2 marks)

53. Give two examples each of vertebrates and invertebrates, and state one feature of each group. (4 marks)

54. Describe how to investigate the effect of different surfaces on friction using a ramp and a block. Include what you keep the same. (5 marks)

55. State two functions of roots. (2 marks)

56. A tap leaks 4 litres every hour. How much water is lost in 6 hours? (2 marks)

57. Name two roots, two stems and two leaves that people eat. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Water, air and light
   Plants need water, air, light and nutrients from the soil.

2. B — Plants show life by growing and responding
   Plants show many signs of life even though they do not walk.

3. B — Tiny holes
   Air moves in and out of leaves through tiny holes.

4. D — Pulls its body into its shell
   This is a response to touch.

5. D — Eating too fast or germs in dirty food
   Fast eating and dirty food can cause stomach pain.

6. C — Kills worms in the intestines
   Deworming tablets kill worms living in the intestines.

7. D — Anus
   Waste leaves the body through the anus.

8. A — Mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine
   Food goes from the mouth down the gullet to the stomach and then the small intestine.

9. D — It has a fixed volume but no fixed shape
   A liquid has a fixed volume and takes the container's shape.

10. C — Oxygen
   Oxygen in the air is needed for life.

11. D — The amount of space an object takes up
   Volume is the space a substance takes up.

12. A — They can be poured and swallowed
   Liquids pour easily.

13. A — 1250 g
   1 kg = 1000 g, and 1000 + 250 = 1250 g.

14. C — Gas
   Gases spread out to fill all the space.

15. C — It makes reusing, recycling and composting easier
   Sorting helps each type be managed properly.

16. B — Waste that rots and breaks down
   Decomposable waste is broken down by decomposers.

17. D — It blocks drains and causes floods
   Waste blocks drains and water floods the area.

18. B — They protect the feet from sharp things and dirt
   Boots protect feet from cuts and germs.

19. B — Carrying a cloth shopping bag
   A reusable bag means fewer plastic bags are thrown away.

20. C — Use a basin
   Using a basin limits the water used.

21. B — 20 litres
   5 x 4 = 20 litres.

22. C — Gives water to each plant a drop at a time
   It gives water slowly at the roots.

23. C — Close the tap after use
   A short, clear message helps people remember.

24. D — 72 litres
   3 x 24 = 72 litres.

25. D — Fresh water is limited
   Only a small part of the world's water is fresh and usable.

26. B — Cutting trees near it and wasting water
   Cutting trees near sources reduces water.

27. D — It uses less water
   A bucket has a limited amount of water.

28. D — Cleaning used water so it can be used again
   Recycling cleans water for another use.

29. C — It moves slowly with the gentle push
   A bigger force gives a bigger effect.

30. D — It speeds up
   A force in the direction of movement increases speed.

31. C — The wheel reduces friction
   Wheels roll and reduce friction.

32. A — To give light in the dark
   A torch is an artificial light source.

33. D — Firefly
   Fireflies make their own light.

34. A — Electric bulbs
   Bulbs are artificial light.

35. D — Shine when car lights fall on them
   Reflectors bounce light back.

36. B — It reflects light from the sun
   The moon does not make its own light.

37. D — Using gloves
   Gloves give protection.

38. A — It loses heat to the air and cup
   Heat goes from the tea to the cooler surroundings.

39. B — Keeps them warm under her wings
   Chicks need warmth.

40. B — So it does not rot or grow mould
   Heat dries the grain and dry grain keeps longer.

SECTION B
----
41. (5 marks)
   Answer: Use windows and translucent sheets by day, solar lamps and LED bulbs at night, keep candles and paraffin away from cloth, turn off lights when not needed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 5.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Natural: stars, lightning, firefly. Artificial: candle, torch, solar lamp.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair, plus 1 mark for correct table.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wear gloves and closed shoes, use a rake or shovel, do not touch sharp objects, wash hands afterwards, do not burn waste.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose thick cotton cloth or old towel. Trace and cut two mitten shapes. Add an inner layer. Sew them together leaving the wrist open. Turn it inside out.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: Wet two similar cloths. Hang one in the sun and the other in the shade. After some time, feel them. The cloth in the sun dries faster because heat from the sun evaporates the water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 mark for method, 1 mark for fair comparison, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for conclusion.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use a torch in a dark room. Put tissue paper, clear plastic and a book one at a time between the torch and a wall. Record whether all, some or no light passes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for equipment, 1 mark for method, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for classification.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Each grain of sand is a small solid with its own shape. The grains are piled together and pour as a pile.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for grains being solids, 1 mark for grains having shape, 1 mark for conclusion.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Chewed in the mouth, swallowed, pushed down the gullet, churned in the stomach, digested and absorbed in the small intestine, water taken back in the large intestine, faeces stored in the rectum and passed out of the anus.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for every two correct steps up to 4.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: To have enough water for all, to save money, for crops and animals, to protect sources.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sorting separates plastics, metals, glass, paper and food waste so each can be recycled, reused or composted without contaminating the others.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sorting, 1 mark for recycling, 1 mark for composting, 1 mark for clear link.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Never look directly at the sun, do not shine torches in eyes, keep candles and lamps away from curtains and paper, do not touch hot bulbs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: A vertebrate has a backbone and an invertebrate has no backbone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Vertebrates: goat and tilapia, have a backbone. Invertebrates: ant and snail, have no backbone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two vertebrates, 1 mark for feature, 1 mark for two invertebrates, 1 mark for feature.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: Make a ramp. Slide a block down it covered with cloth, paper, cardboard and bare board. Measure how far it slides each time. Keep the same block, same ramp height and same push. Record in a table. The shortest distance shows the most friction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for ramp, 1 mark for surfaces, 1 mark for measuring, 1 mark for fair test, 1 mark for conclusion.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: They hold the plant in the soil and take in water and mineral salts. Some store food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct function.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: 24 litres.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4 x 6 and 1 mark for the answer with units.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Roots: carrot, cassava, sweet potato. Stems: sugarcane. Leaves: cabbage, sukuma wiki, spinach (any two of each, with correct grouping).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair and 1 mark for correct grouping overall.
